human_memory:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: pixel-art material and face sheet for a Minecraft Java 64x64 human skin, to import onto an ordinary slim female player mesh.
Primary request: a sad, exhausted young human woman inspired by the grieving girl in Stephen Graham Jones's Indian Lake story; humanity and hurt, rather than monstrous imagery.
Composition: exactly four equal square quadrants, without gaps or borders. Top left: a perfectly square front-facing face in an 8 by 8 pixel grid, warm medium brown skin, dark tired eyes, straight dark brown bangs, small closed mouth; no neck, no background, the face fills the entire quadrant. Top right: a seamless tile of wet, straight dark chestnut hair. Bottom left: seamless tile of faded blue cotton shirt, wet creases, subtle frayed fabric. Bottom right: seamless tile of muddy charcoal skirt fabric. Flat unlit albedo, simple restrained pixel art, hard square pixels.
Constraints: no lettering, labels, watermark, weapons, claws, fangs, horns, glowing eyes, skeletal features, green skin, open mouth or blood. The face should look like a real hurting girl, not a monster. Square sheet.
transformed_witch:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: hunting-form material sheet for the Lake Witch, a Minecraft horror NPC. This sheet will be imported onto the same character mesh as the human memory skin.
Edit target: the supplied four-quadrant sheet. Preserve all quadrant boundaries, straight-on flat albedo, pixel-art style and the recognizable young girl's face, eyes, nose, hair and faded clothing. Change her to a plainly supernatural revenant: cold grey-brown bloodless skin over her original brown complexion, deep almost black eye sockets with tiny cloudy eyes, gaunt cheeks, dark water streaks and mud around the face, a slightly parted blackened mouth with a small irregular line of pale teeth. Wet hair tangled across one eye. Her expression is uncanny and frightening, with grief still visible. Her hunting form is a girl who became a monster, not a normal sad girl.
Top right: darken the wet hair and tangle a few strands. Bottom left: make the same blue shirt ragged and lake-stained, frayed seams and tiny dark torn patches. Bottom right: make the same charcoal skirt stained with silt and dried dark reddish marks. No horns, giant fangs, hat, green zombie skin, glowing fantasy eyes, new accessories, text, border or watermark. The original normal girl remains the memory; this is her transformed monster variant.
shared_cast_materials:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: one shared Minecraft NPC material texture atlas, used to retexture the remaining authored NPC meshes while preserving their individual faces and exact UVs.
Primary request: a square, flat, unlit pixel-art textile and creature-material atlas with eight equal tiles in a 4-column by 2-row grid, no gaps. Each tile must be a seamless, completely filled repeating albedo material, not a character, object or illustration.
Top row left to right: faded burgundy wool shawl with worn seams; old dark floral skirt cloth in dusty brown and plum; faded mustard cotton shirt with tiny subtle fabric checks; desaturated olive blue plaid flannel shirt.
Bottom row left to right: an antique charcoal wool coat with fine weave; cream linen blouse with worn yellowing; long, rough dark brown bull fur with chestnut strands; soft chestnut and cream dog fur with a few darker strands.
Style: restrained blocky pixel art suited to Minecraft's tiny native NPC skin atlas. Distinct legible material grain and ordinary clothes. No text, labels, faces, borders, background or watermarks. Keep it flat and evenly lit; no baked highlights or shadows. Material detail should survive shrinking each tile to 16x16 pixels.
